Log a debug message, if the log level is `debug` or higher.

## Signature

```typescript
debug(message?: unknown, ...args: unknown[]): void;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

message


</td><td>

unknown


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Message to log, as accepted by `util.format()`<!-- -->. If  omitted or `undefined`<!-- -->, it is replaced by an empty string (see  <b>Empty messages</b> in the description of the class).


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

args


</td><td>

unknown\[\]


</td><td>

Optional variable arguments.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Returns

void

## Remarks

The message is prefixed with `debug: ` and passed via `console.log()`<!-- -->. If the logger was created with the `timestamp` option, it starts with a timestamp, and the prefix is replaced by `[debug]`<!-- -->. An `Error` object is expanded with the full stack trace and the `cause` chain, on several lines, and the prefix is kept, even when the error is the first argument (`debug: Error: boom`<!-- -->, followed by the stack trace; see <b>The prefix of an <code>Error</code></b> in the description of the class).

## Example


```javascript
log.debug(`spawn: ${cmd}`)
```
